Subject: POC workshop & load-run orchestration for ACME — timing and test-harness prep

Hi Liz,

Thanks again for taking the demo last week. Per our conversation, we'd like to schedule the hands-on POC workshop that combines:
- a 30–45m prompt review + routing/priority rules session,
- a 45–60m load/benchmark run (throughput targets + latency SLO verification), and
- a short wrap with rollout/checklist items.

What we need from ACME ahead of the session:
- target throughput: expected peak QPS or messages/sec and average tokens per response (approx),
- representative prompt set (short list is fine) — I attached a template,
- any IP/network constraints so we can pre-authorize test endpoints.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Thu Jun 25: 10:00–12:00 (hands-on + run)
- Fri Jun 26: 09:00–11:30 (longer run, spare buffer)
- Mon Jun 29: 13:00–15:00 (if you prefer afternoon)

We're bringing: Vivek (infrastructure lead) and Marissa (account lead) to run the harness and coordinate results. I attached a draft runbook and a starter harness config — please drop your prompt CSV into the attached template and return it; we'll ingest it into the harness before the session.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (template), test-harness-config.yml (sample), poc-runbook-draft.pdf

Best,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Thanks Jordan — this looks great.

Quick notes:
- Peak throughput: we expect up to 380 QPS during promos, average response ~ 90 tokens (we'll validate). For safety, can we plan the run to target 450 QPS as an upper bound?
- Network: our infra team needs IPs for allowlist; I can get a short-lived CIDR list from them by EOD Thursday.
- Prompts: Sam and I will populate the CSV by Thursday morning.

About timing — Friday Jun 26 is tight for us (leadership meeting), but Thu Jun 25 10:00 works if we can keep the run shorter (target run 45m). Can Vivek drop the intensity ramp plan so we can see early failure modes?

Thanks — Liz
Liz Harper

Subject: Re: POC workshop & load-run orchestration for ACME — timing and test-harness prep

Jordan — noted. I'll bring a conservative ramp plan (below) and the harness will emit token-level latency histograms + 95th/99th percentiles in real time. If ACME can provide a short-lived allowlist CIDR we can avoid handshake delays.

Planned ramp (config to attach to invite):
- Smoke: 200 quick queries over 2 minutes (routing + KV warm)
- Ramp1: 0 -> 120 QPS over 6 minutes (linear)
- Ramp2: 120 -> 320 QPS over 8 minutes (linear)
- Peak hold: 450 QPS for 10 minutes (if ACME approves)
- Cooldown: back to 50 QPS over 5 minutes

Metrics we will collect:
- per-second QPS, avg token/service latency, 50/95/99 latencies, token cost breakdown, error rates by model variant.

I'll attach the explicit harness YAML with knobs (concurrency, client-side pacing, model pins).

—Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: test-harness-config.yml
